name: E. Elmer
role: Medora businessman; justice of the peace elected 1886
bio: E. Elmer brought his family from Jamestown in October 1884 and opened a new place of business in Medora that November. In 1885 he built a house and veneered it with brick, and on Christmas morning 1884 someone set burning hay between his building and Gill Kennedy's. He ran for justice of the peace on both the Billings County and Stockmen's tickets in spring 1886, won with 121 votes, and had his bond accepted in May. In September 1886 the paper announced a baby daughter.

moments.label: Prepared to open his new Medora business
Elected justice of the peace with 121 votes

mentions: Mr. E. Elmer's family arrived from Jamestown on Wednesday. Mr. Elmer will open up a place of business on the other side of the river.
E. Elmer is busily engaged in preparing his new place of business. He expects to open up next Monday.

Some despicable villain put a bundle of lighted hay between the buildings occupied by Gill Kennedy and E. Elmer, Christmas morning. It may have been done as a joke, but it would have been a choke if the perpetrator had been discovered.
E. Elmer is building a dwelling house on Williamson & Copeland's lot.
E. Elmer has veneered his cottage with brick and is now ready to go into winter quarters.
